definition: Predicting missing facts in a knowledge graph — inferring (entity, relation, entity) triples — with embedding models like TransE and RotatE or LM-based scorers.
details: Predicting missing facts in a knowledge graph — inferring (entity, relation, entity) triples — with embedding models like TransE and RotatE or LM-based scorers.

explainer.lead: Knowledge graph completion fills in facts a knowledge graph is missing, predicting triples that were never recorded. It matters because real graphs are incomplete, and many downstream queries depend on facts nobody has entered yet.

tiers.eli5: Think of a friendship map with some lines missing; completion draws the likely lines between people who probably know each other.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train embedding models like TransE or RotatE, or score triples with language models, then rank candidate facts for review. A common pitfall is over-trusting high scores on popular entities, so predictions need validation before being written back.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a graph of (entity, relation, entity) triples, learn a scoring function f(h, r, t) that rates how plausible a triple is, then rank unseen triples by that score; accuracy on rare relations is typically the limiting factor.

explainer.example: A graph knows Paris is the capital of France and Lyon is in France but lacks a direct link; a model scores (Lyon, capital_of, France) low and (Lyon, located_in, France) high, so the latter is proposed.
